summary: Nonlinear tier applied to mixed-sequence multi-model batch leading to unexpected invoice charge
description: Customer reports a surprise invoice where a single multi-model batch job (mixed short and long sequences) was billed using a nonlinear higher tier multiplier instead of the expected weighted per-token rate. The customer expects per-token weighting across model variants; instead, a peak-sequence tier was applied to the entire job resulting in ~3.8x higher charge than estimate.
impact: Immediate unexpected charge on finalized invoice for March cycle. Customer has paused scheduled overnight batch runs. This affects billing reconciliation and forecasting for a large healthcare data-processing job (sensitive to month-end budgeting).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs mixed-model batch job 'synth-qa-2026-02-28' using two models: mixseq-embedder-v2 (short sequences ~32 tokens) and dialog-2b-multi (long sequences up to 6k tokens).
2) Job submitted through Dedicated queue (pool-dedicated-us-east-3).
3) Postback stream shows per-request token_count and sequence_length_bucket.
4) Finalized invoice shows line item with rate multiplier matching >4096 token tier applied to entire job instead of per-model weighting.
logs:
Postback sample (sanitized): request_id=rp_9f2a7, timestamp=2026-02-28T03:14:22Z, model=dialog-2b-multi, token_count=6120, sequence_length_bucket=">4096"; request_id=rp_9f2a8, model=mixseq-embedder-v2, token_count=28, sequence_length_bucket="<64".
Billing reconciler entries: postback_ingest_id=ing_2026_8721 (ingest window 2026-02-28T00:00-04:00), computed_rate_key=rate_tier:>4096 (applied_total_tokens=1,148,236).
Invoice line: invoice_2026_03_line_44: rate_code=hybrid-multi-tier, applied_multiplier=3.8x, description='Hybrid batch mixed - applied peak-tier'.
initial_investigation_notes:
- Billing team reproduced mapping of postback->tier: mapping logic currently buckets per-job by max(sequence_length_bucket) rather than per-request aggregation.
- Postback replays show the reconstructor aggregated token counts across models but then looked up rate_tier using the single highest sequence bin seen in the job window.
- Potential contributing factor: an async ingest rewrite deployed 2026-02-20 (PR #487) that changed the order of per-request normalization and job-level aggregation.
- Tokenizer inconsistency flagged: dialog-2b-multi returns additional control tokens for tool-calls; these were double-counted in the aggregator during the ingest rewrite (token_count inflated by ~2-4% for long items).
hypothesis: The postback ingest change (PR 487) inadvertently changed the aggregation order: instead of summing per-request charges and weighting by model, the pipeline computed the job-level maximum sequence bucket and applied that bucket's rate to the whole job. This explains the non-linear 'peak-tier' application. Tokenizer control-token duplication exacerbated the bucketization for long sequences pushing the job into >4096 bin.
workaround:
1) Temporary manual reclassification of invoice lines for job 'synth-qa-2026-02-28' to per-request weighted rate (billing adjustment).
2) Customer should re-run future jobs with an annotation header 'metering-mode: per-request' (we can accept this header and force the correct aggregation until fix deploys).
proposed_fix: Revert aggregation order in postback-reconciler to compute per-request effective token units, aggregate costs by weighted sum, then map to invoice tiers. Add guard in pipeline to ignore job-level max-bucket lookups for mixed-model batches. Patch scheduled: 2026-03-05; rolling deploy with canary on a small set of dedicated pools.
resolution: Credits pending: provisional credit issued equal to delta between billed amount and expected weighted amount for invoice_2026_03 (credit memo CM-78291 created). Permanent fix scheduled and tracked in INT-9271. We will reprocess affected ingestion window and adjust any additional customers impacted before next billing cut.
follow_up_tasks:
- INT-9271: Postback aggregator order revert and unit tests (owner: infra-ingest).
- Billing: run reconciliation job to find other invoices with 'applied_multiplier>2' for Feb 20-28 window.
- DX: add customer-facing metering doc snippet describing mixed-model batch semantics.
customer_message: Hi — thanks for flagging this. We traced the overcharge to a regression in our postback ingestion that caused a peak-tier to be applied at the job level. We've created a provisional credit for the March invoice and scheduled a fix to the invoicing pipeline. We'll notify you when the fix is deployed and after we've reprocessed the affected window. Apologies for the disruption and thank you for pausing the overnight jobs while we resolve this.
